concepts.label: managed-object
concepts.gloss: A managed-object is an identifiable network resource or element whose operational state is monitored and against which events and alarms are raised.
concepts.example: The optical resource lambda1 is the managed object on which trap-lambda1-t0 occurs and alarm-lambda1-SD is raised.

concepts.label: event
concepts.gloss: An event is a point-in-time notification, such as a syslog message or SNMP trap, reporting an occurrence observed on a managed object without necessarily representing a persistent fault condition.
concepts.example: trap-lambda1-t0 is an event emitted for the managed object lambda1 at time t0.

concepts.label: alarm
concepts.gloss: An alarm is a fault-condition record associated with a managed object that carries a perceived severity and a probable-cause code and remains relevant until cleared or otherwise resolved.
concepts.example: alarm-lambda1-SD records a degraded-signal fault on lambda1, carrying severity major and probable cause degradedSignal.

concepts.label: severity
concepts.gloss: Severity is the perceived impact or urgency classification assigned to an alarm, using levels such as critical, major, minor, or warning.
concepts.example: alarm-lambda1-SD carries the severity major, indicating a more serious condition than minor or warning but below critical.

concepts.label: probable-cause
concepts.gloss: A probable-cause is the standardized X.733-style cause code carried by an alarm to identify the type of fault believed to have produced the alarm condition.
concepts.example: alarm-lambda1-SD carries degradedSignal as its probable cause, distinguishing it from a lossOfSignal fault.

concepts.label: clear
concepts.gloss: A clear is a lifecycle notification or record that terminates a specific previously raised alarm because its associated fault condition is no longer active.
concepts.example: clear-lambda1-SD clears alarm-lambda1-SD after the degraded-signal condition on lambda1 has ended.
